answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every new identity to lock a time-seasoned bond in a shared grove of already-established peers; a detected clone slashes the whole deposit. Endorsements then form a vine that only those bonded peers can extend, and each link expires unless refreshed with a costly countersignature. Incoming jobs enter a harbor that admits traffic solely from identities whose vine remains intact and whose grove bond is unslashed, so mass-spawned aliases starve for work before they recoup the bond.
